forecaster_note: Building SSW–S groundswell through the day. Small and clean at dawn (2–3ft, only 85 kJ at 9am) then the new pulse arrives from late morning — 5.1ft @ 9s from 180° pushing 278 kJ by midday and 387 kJ by mid-afternoon. W–WSW offshore holds until roughly 11am before going light variable and then ESE onshore from about 2pm. The catch is the angle: 180° is dead south, so the size lands on the south-facing banks and largely misses Dee Why. — compiled from Surfline forecast data (Surfline forecaster note not available this refresh)

wind.summary: W–WSW offshore 10–11kph with 22kph gusts from dawn to about 11am, then dropping to 5kph light S around midday and swinging ESE onshore 8kph from roughly 2–3pm. The clean window closes at lunchtime.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW live layers (DPI Fisheries + SLSNSW drone) were read successfully this refresh, but the most recent entry in both feeds is dated 25 July — the detection feed has not updated in 18 days, so no all-clear can be given. Tap through to check live detections before you paddle out.

days.label: Today
days.note: A building day, not a peaking one. Dawn is clean but gutless — 85 kJ at 9am off a 3.9ft @ 6s SSW slop swell. The real pulse lands late morning: 5.1ft @ 9s from 180° taking energy to 278 kJ by midday and 387 kJ by 3pm. Your 10am–12pm slot sits right on the ramp with the last of the W–WSW offshore and a draining tide off the 8:36am high. Go at 10, not 8. The angle is dead south again, so Long Reef is where that energy actually lands.

dee-why.window: 10am–12pm. Waits for the swell to fill in, still has offshore, tide draining off the 8:36am high. Before 10 it's thigh-to-waist and slow.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point — but be patient
tip.text: 387 kJ is the day's headline and it is mostly the 5.1ft @ 9s at 180°. Dead south is your worst angle here — it wraps in fat and walls up rather than bowling. The 2.1ft @ 10s from 76° is the component with a shoulder on it. Sit off the Point, let the south sets go by and take the ENE-angled ones for your frontside rights. At 9am there is only 85 kJ in the water, so arriving early is arriving to nothing.

alerts: Dead-south 180° — the size does not translate here
ESE onshore from ~2pm

long-reef.window: 10am–1pm. The pick of the four by a clear margin — 4–6ft by midday with the offshore still holding.

tip.label: Go here — the south magnet
tip.text: 3–4ft at 9am becomes 4–6ft by midday and 5–7ft by mid-afternoon, on the same energy Dee Why is only turning into 3–4ft. That is 180° swinging straight into it. 9s is workable spacing rather than the 6s slop of first light, and the W–WSW offshore holds until about 11am. This is the session today. Watch the drop to the 2:16pm low if you push late.

alerts: Biggest of the four — expect solid sets by midday
ESE onshore from ~2pm

curl-curl.window: 10:30am–1pm. Doubles in size between 9am and midday — 2–3ft becomes 4–5ft. Look before you commit.

tip.label: The bank lottery
tip.text: Curl Curl takes this south angle almost as well as Long Reef — 2–3ft at 9am, 4–5ft by noon, 4–6ft by 3pm. On a 9s period with a dropping tide the north end usually holds the better shape. If Long Reef has a crowd this is the backup, but the sand decides it.

alerts: Closeout risk once it hits 4–6ft on a 9s south
ESE onshore from ~2pm

manly.window: Only if you want something easy — 2–3ft until mid-afternoon, 3–4ft after 3pm once the wind has already turned.

tip.label: Backside on the lefts
tip.text: North Steyne is the most shadowed of the four from 180° and it shows — stuck at 2–3ft through the whole clean window while Long Reef is 4–6ft. The size only arrives at 3pm, by which time the ESE onshore has it. Fine for a soft backhand paddle, wrong call if you want waves.

alerts: Smallest of the four — sheltered from the south
Size only arrives after the wind turns onshore

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Straight dawn patrol. The swell peaks overnight and eases all day — 229 kJ at 6am down to 102 kJ by 3pm — so first light is the biggest and cleanest it gets. Light W offshore 5–6kph until about 11am, then ESE onshore from early afternoon. In the water by 7am or don't bother.

dee-why.window: 6:30–9am. 3–4ft at dawn easing to 2–3ft by midday — the earlier the better, and the light 5kph W is barely enough to hold it up.
alerts: Easing all day — 229 kJ at dawn, 102 kJ by 3pm
ESE onshore from ~1pm

long-reef.window: 6:30–9:30am. Holds 3–4ft the longest of the four as the swell drops off.
alerts: ESE onshore from ~1pm

curl-curl.window: 7–9am. Best of the four at 9am if the bank is holding — 3–4ft with light W offshore.
alerts: ESE onshore from ~1pm

manly.window: Dawn only, and it is 2–3ft the whole way. Skip unless it is convenience over quality.
alerts: Smallest of the four again
ESE onshore from ~1pm

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the day and it is a builder, same shape as today. Small at dawn (77 kJ), filling through the morning to 226 kJ by midday and 330 kJ by 3pm, with light W–SW offshore until about 11am before the S wind arrives. Your 10am–1pm slot catches the build with the wind still workable. Sunday collapses — 8–10kph E/ESE onshore from first light and energy halved to 184 kJ. Plan Saturday.

dee-why.window: Sat 10am–1pm on the build. Sunday is onshore from dawn — write it off.
alerts: S swell angle again — size lands elsewhere
Sat: S wind fills in from ~11am
Sun: E/ESE onshore 8–10kph all day

long-reef.window: Sat 10am–1pm — 3–4ft at 9am becoming 4–6ft by mid-afternoon. The weekend session.
alerts: Sat: S wind 7–10kph from midday
Sun: 4–6ft but onshore and gutless at 184 kJ

curl-curl.window: Sat late morning if the bank is good. Sunday onshore all day.
alerts: Closeout risk on the bigger Sat afternoon sets
Sun: E/ESE onshore from dawn

manly.window: Sat mid-morning only. Most sheltered, so smallest, but it holds shape longest once the S fills in.
alerts: Smallest of the four both days
